To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The formalism presented here provides a simple, consistent, and efficient way of studying the nonequilibrium evolution of coupled scalar field models, (ii) The formalism is applicable to any scalar model, and (iii) In particular, we have studied the dynamics of a simple two-field inflation model and a supersymmetric hybrid model.

(i) The dynamics of coupled, multi-field models can be described by an effective Lagrangian that incorporates the evolution of the mean fields, and their associated fluctuations, at one-loop order; (ii) In the case of reheating, the evolution of the energy density in the fluctuations is governed by a set of coupled, non-linear, second order differential equations.

the evolution of the fluctuations of a multi-field system during preheating is determined by a renormalization group equation which includes the back reaction of the fluctuations on the evolution of the mean fields.

the study of the evolution of a system of coupled, interacting scalar fields.
the development of methods to study the nonequilbrium dynamics of coupled scalar field theories.
the dynamics of coupled scalar models in the context of preheating and inflationary reheating.
